text: Rust allows only one mutable reference at a time so a value cannot be changed through two aliases at once, which would let one reference invalidate the memory or assumptions the other still relies on. That rule prevents data races and the broader class of memory-safety bugs from aliased mutation, such as iterator invalidation and use-after-free.
thought:
The user is asking a conceptual question about Rust's borrow checker.

Rust enforces exclusive mutable access to prevent data races and undefined behavior from aliased mutation.

This also prevents iterator invalidation and dangling pointers from concurrent mutation.

The rule is called exclusive mutability. It also enables compiler optimizations based on noalias.
